title: World Cup 2026 Venues Guide: A Tour of All 16 Stadiums
summary: A comprehensive guide to the 16 stadiums across the United States, Canada, and Mexico hosting the first-ever 48-team FIFA World Cup.
content:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup makes history as the first tournament spread across three nations, with 16 world-class stadiums in the United States, Canada, and Mexico playing host. Here is your complete guide to every venue welcoming the world's finest footballers this summer.

United States Venues

MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, takes center stage as the venue for the final, boasting a capacity of 82,500. AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, brings its retractable roof and 80,000 seats to the party. SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, offers cutting-edge technology and a 70,000 capacity. Other American venues include Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, NRG Stadium in Houston, Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Lumen Field in Seattle, Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, and Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City.

Canadian Hosts

Canada contributes two outstanding venues to the tournament. BMO Field in Toronto has been expanded to 45,000 seats for the occasion, while BC Place in Vancouver offers a 54,000-capacity stadium with a retractable roof perfectly suited to the Pacific Northwest climate. Both venues have undergone significant renovations to meet FIFA's exacting standards for pitch dimensions, broadcast facilities, and supporter infrastructure.

Mexico's Iconic Stadiums

Mexico brings unmatched World Cup pedigree with three venues. The legendary Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, hosting its third World Cup, remains one of football's most iconic grounds with a capacity of 87,000. Estadio BBVA in Monterrey and Estadio Akron in Guadalajara complete the Mexican contingent, both modern arenas that have hosted major international fixtures in recent years.

Sustainability and Innovation

FIFA has placed sustainability at the heart of venue operations, with all 16 stadiums committed to carbon-neutral match days. Solar panels, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and zero-waste catering initiatives have been implemented across every ground. The transportation plans connecting stadiums to city centers feature expanded public transit and dedicated shuttle services to minimize the tournament's environmental footprint.
